chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad ibn Uthman, and others, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Poetry (or recitation) should not be sought/recited at night, nor should it be sought/recited during the month of Ramadan at night or by day.
So Ismail said to him, 'O my father! Indeed, it is among us.'
He said, 'And even if it is among us.'

key_terms.فِينَا: Among us (referring to the Ahl al-Bayt or Imams)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on reciting poetry during Ramadan according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes a general etiquette of spiritual restraint during Ramadan, prohibiting the recitation of poetry even if it is virtuous or from the Ahl al-Bayt, to preserve the solemnity of the month. This ruling highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on *adab* (etiquette) and minimizing worldly distractions, ensuring that the heart remains focused on worship and contemplation rather than aesthetic appreciation. The confirmation 'even if it is among us' underscores that the prohibition is rooted in the sanctity of the time rather than the content's merit.
